VISA Experience 
   
 
2
 
 
Overview: 
This was the first time that VISA was coming to our campus, so it came as a bit of surprise to us and yeah it 
also got us a little excited for the company. 
 
So as there was no prior experience about the company in our archive, we had to do some digging for the 
company and the best place to do it was none another than GeeksforGeeks. So, I read all the archives from GFG 
and this was the summary 
1. They had 2 Rounds in order to get an internship, first was Online Coding Round (Conventionally 2 DSA 
Problems will be given to solve in 1 hour), second round was mainly technical but they also ask a few 
HR Questions (the HR Questions are generally just to test how much excited are u for the company, so 
this a general tip: always show excitement/enthusiasm/confidence in HR Round). 
2. They mainly ask Dynamic Programming, Graph, Backtracking, Heap and Recursion so to sum up, 
prepare DSA thoroughly. 
 
After reading all the articles, I contacted some of their previous interns from other colleges through Linkedin 
and they also fed me the same experience as above. In fact, one guy told me that his interviewer gave him four 
DSA questions to solve and said if u solve them then you are selected no further questions asked (but again it is 
not NECESSARY that it will happen to you too!!). 
 
 
 
8th Sept 2022 – Pre-Placement Talk 
They held their PPT on Microsoft teams. 
Note down their Mission/Principles/Values/Vision cuz these are the things that you’ll be needing in HR Round. 
 
 
 
9th Sept 2022 – First Round (Online Assessment) 
It was conducted on Hackerank where everyone was allotted a different pair of DSA problems and the time 
limit was an hour. We weren’t the only ones that were giving the test, but IIT Gandhinagar (as far as I 
remember) was also scheduled parallelly so the toughness of pool of those questions was from medium to hard. 
 
Tip: Try to solve any Online Assessment as soon as possible, if it contains only Coding Questions then it’s a big 
plus plus, but if the OA also contains MCQs then please don’t end up giving wrong answers in hurry.

VISA Experience 
   
 
5
13th Sept – 2nd Round (Technical Round + HR Round for 1 hour) 
The Interviewer directly dived into my projects and started asking questions on them (no tell me about yourself 
questions were asked). Some of the general questions were: 
a) Motive for building the project? 
b) Reason for using this particular Tech Stack? 
 
For the project part, be prepared with everything such as Github, Online Database (if you are using any), etc. 
They may ask you to open it and present it in the meet. 
There were other questions also but they were specifically related to my project so they won’t help you much… 
 
So basically, we had conversation on my projects for almost 30 to 40 min and NO DSA questions were asked in 
the interview xD and because of this I had neutral feelings :/ cuz I was hoping at least a couple of DSA 
questions thrown in my way, but later it turned out that the interviewer was a project manager and was into 
managing teams and stuff so yup, this was kinda expected from a person at that position.  
 
Then she asked me a general question on how would you keep a record of the peoples who borrowed a book 
from a hypothetical library that you owned. 
I started designing a sql database for the situation and then there were some follow up questions on sql queries 
for the designed database. 
 
Then she asked a few questions on Core CS Subjects, they were on (I don’t remember most of them, but their 
toughness was on medium level): 
a) Deadlock 
b) How to prevent Deadlock 
c) Process, Threads (if you know java then you should also prepare multithreading) 
Then she moved onto HR part and asked these standard questions: 
a) Why Visa? 
b) One Moment in your life where you’ve done something extraordinary? 
(there were other questions too, but these are the ones that I remember) 
 
Then she asked, what were the current technologies that I was learning to which I replied that, “currently I am 
not learning any new tech stuff but rather I was focusing on my DSA skills from a past few months, cuz you can 
learn new technologies within a couple of weeks (if given time) but before that you need to have a strong basic 
foundation for Computer Science and its core subjects”. Now this was the part which got her impressed xD and 
she replied positively with a smile :) 
 
(If you’ve cleared your Online Assessment for any interview then remember this, your interviewers are simply 
looking for some people who are excited to join their firm, who are enthusiastic to work as a team, who have a 
strong basic foundation, who are eager to learn new stuff plus a little smile on your face is a cherry on the cake 
:) 
 
Then she asked me if I had any questions, do ask questions, it shows your interest in their firm. 
Then she asked if I had any seniors who has experience as VISA interns. I told her that VISA came to our 
campus for the first time, to which she replied that it’s not possible because she had some members working on 
her team from VJTI and after some more chat we ended our meet. 
 
Now in my interview, no DSA questions were asked but you should be thoroughly prepared for DSA. 
Then at night, results came and they hired 4 interns and I was lucky enough to be one among them :)

VISA Experience 
   
 
6
Resources: 
 
DSA: 
First of all, I prepared the basics through Abdul Bari’s Course of DSA on Udemy. Then I moved on to 
algorithms and started solving problems  
1. I religiously solved leetcode’s problem of the day and solved TOP 100 Liked Questions. 
2. I followed 450 DSA too. 
 
Operating System: 
I completed Gate Smasher’s playlist, studied notes of Apni Kaksha and also went through 40 Interview Bits 
Questions. 
1. Gate Smashers 
2. Apni Kaksha 
3. Interview Bits 
4. Operating System Frequently Asked Questions 
 
Difference between Semaphore and Mutex: 
1. Difference between Semaphore and Mutex Part 1 
2. Difference between Semaphore and Mutex Part 2 
3. Difference between Semaphore and Mutex Part 3 
 
 
DBMS: 
I completed Sachit Jains Playlist and went through Apni Kaksha Notes thoroughly (especially for queries) and 
then I went for Interview Bit’s notes: 
1. Sanchit Jain 
2. Apni Kaksha 
3. Interview Bits 
(Tip: Prepare queries thoroughly and some theoretical topics of DBMS like ACID props) 
 
Object Oriented Programming:  
I prepared OOP in my first year, so only some revision was needed on imp topics 
1. Code With Harry (only if you have time) 
2. Javapoint Tutorials (If you don’t have much time then this is the perfect source to study OOPs 
thoroughly) 
3. Apni Kaksha 
4. Interview Bits 
(Tip: Don’t just read it, cuz you might be asked to implement some class or give the output of some given code 
which consists of virtual function, abstract class and what not) 
 
Computer Networks (Interviewers generally don’t ask questions from this part, so prepare only if you 
have an ample amount of time): 
1. Apni Kaksha  
2. Gate Smashers 
 
HR  
Interview Bit

VISA Experience 
   
 
7
 
 
 
Tips for Technical Round: 
1. Smile. 
2. Be Confident. 
3. In any condition, don’t be silent, that puts a bad impression on the interviewer, so keep talking about 
whatever the things that you know about the topic and explaining your topic with real life examples is a 
big plus plus. 
4. THINK OUT LOUD. The interviewers are not mind readers... so talk. Tell them honestly even if you are 
not sure about your solution. IT IS OKAY to tell them if you don’t know everything or you are not able 
to solve the problem completely. Your approach and way of thinking is judged mostly. (Silence here 
won’t help you) 
5. If the Interview is in offline mode and they have provided you pen and paper, then fill those sheets with 
whatever that comes in your mind, be it code for some of the naivest question they asked, a simple class 
diagram (for dbms), architecture of your project, etc (just don’t keep it blank :). 
6. If the Interview is in online mode, then you can use paint (or any other tool) for explaining stuff e.g. 
how your project works, etc. 
7. Make it look like an interactive discussion rather than Q & A round. 
 
 
Tips for HR Round: 
1. Smile. 
2. Be Confident. 
3. Prepare general questions like: 
a) Why <company_name>? 
b) Why should <company_name> hire you? 
c) Any extra-ordinary moment in your life? 
4. Interview Bit 
5. Do some research about the firm and their mission/aim. 
 
(At last, you just want to put an impression on the interviewer that you are hardworking, flexible in situations 
and a quick learner). 
 
Prepare for behavioral questions too. We generally study technical questions and completely ignore 
behavioral questions. 
 
Remember that sometimes things don’t go the way you wished them to.  
So don’t lose hope.  
Don’t give up. 
EVER.  
 
 
 
 
 
All the best, you can do it :) 
For any more queries, feel free to reach me @Linkedin
